SSH Brute-Force & Credential-Stuffing Detector

An interactive Python tool that parses SSH authentication logs and flags brute-force attacks, credential-stuffing attempts, and likely account compromises using sliding-window detection, visualized in a Streamlit dashboard.

Launch the App View on GitHub

What the App Does

  • Log parsing. A regex-based parser reads standard sshd auth log lines — Failed password, Accepted password, and invalid user variants — into a pandas DataFrame.
  • Three detection heuristics, each backed by an O(n) sliding time window:
    • Brute force — repeated failed attempts against a single account from one IP inside a configurable time window.
    • Credential stuffing — failed attempts from one IP spread across many distinct usernames, the bot-style account spraying pattern.
    • Likely compromise — a successful login immediately following a burst of failures from the same IP.
  • Interactive dashboard. Sidebar sliders adjust the threshold and window for every detector, alongside summary metrics, a failed-login timeline, and top offending IPs and usernames. You can upload your own log file or use the bundled synthetic sample, and export flagged IPs to CSV.

How Detection Works

Each detector scans failed-login timestamps for a given IP (and username) with a two-pointer sliding window, finding the maximum number of events inside any window of length N minutes in O(n) time per group. If that count exceeds the threshold, the IP/user pair is flagged.

This mirrors how real detection rules are usually written — “more than 10 failed attempts in 5 minutes” — and the sliders make the tradeoff visible. The sample data includes a deliberately “low and slow” attack that slips past the default settings and only gets caught once the window is widened.

Technical Notes

The project runs on synthetic logs generated by generate_logs.py, which injects the attack patterns into an otherwise ordinary sample_auth.log, so the detectors can be demonstrated without data from a real compromised host. Parsing, detection, and the dashboard are kept in separate modules (log_parser.py, detector.py, dashboard.py) so the detection logic stays independent of the UI.
